# Verification analysis: etcd-member-replacement-centos-stream10

Job: `2026-09-04__19-04-22`

This report explains the verifier decisions recorded for this job. It interprets the saved evidence; it does not rerun the task or independently inspect the expired clusters.

## Task

> Run a three-member etcd cluster across `node1`, `node2`, and `node3` holding
> application keys.
>
> The member on `node3` is permanently lost and its data cannot be recovered.
> Replace it with a working member on that same system so the cluster is back to
> three healthy members with the existing keys intact.

## Trial `etcd-member-replacement-centos-s__t5zEccZ`

**Verifier decision: Full Success.** The executor built a fresh 3-member etcd cluster across node1/node2/node3, loaded application keys, then convincingly simulated a permanent, unrecoverable loss of the node3 member (stop, disable, wipe data) while directly demonstrating node1/node2 retained quorum and node3's endpoint was unhealthy. It then removed the dead member and added/started a genuinely new node3 member with initial-cluster-state=existing, verifying the cluster returned to three healthy 'started' members at a consistent raft index and that all original application keys were present on the resynced node3 member. The independent, provider-mandated node-restart protocol was also completed on all three nodes with clear pre-restart boot-id baselines, restart acknowledgements, changed boot IDs, and confirmed post-restart etcd/cluster/data health, consistent with the fixed after-executor snapshot. The only notable imperfection is leftover installation temp files on all three nodes that were never cleaned up.

| Reward | Coverage | Functionality | Hygiene | Confidence | Commands |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 1.000 | 1.000 | 1.000 | 0.850 | 0.920 | 43/4 (+8 dropped) |

### Why the verifier reached this decision

- **req-1 — Satisfied:** Three-member etcd cluster running across node1, node2, node3 holding application keys
  - **Why:** Cluster bootstrapped with all three members in 'started' state (cmd-dadc8acfa4c543c5); four /app/* keys written on node1 and confirmed present with matching values on node2 and node3 (cmd-fb19ca5f53d347c3, cmd-18edb4fdf5b34271, cmd-11245ee06ecd46cf).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-dadc8acfa4c543c5`, `cmd-fb19ca5f53d347c3`, `cmd-18edb4fdf5b34271`, `cmd-11245ee06ecd46cf`
- **req-2 — Satisfied:** node3 member permanently lost (data unrecoverable) is simulated realistically, with cluster preserving quorum during the outage
  - **Why:** etcd stopped/disabled and /var/lib/etcd wiped on node3 (cmd-fde63ed09f774ceb, cmd-80bee799bbbd47c5); subsequent endpoint health check directly shows node1/node2 healthy while node3's endpoint is unhealthy/connection-refused, demonstrating quorum was retained during the disruption (cmd-1b8d6ad9214840bf).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-fde63ed09f774ceb`, `cmd-80bee799bbbd47c5`, `cmd-1b8d6ad9214840bf`
- **req-3 — Satisfied:** Dead member replaced with a new working member on the same node (node3), cluster restored to three healthy members
  - **Why:** Old member removed via etcdctl (cmd-d2900fdd3d934d1e), new member added and started on node3 with initial-cluster-state=existing (cmd-e0a3fe2633864dd5, cmd-eca00e8542c14fd5); member list and cluster-wide health/status check afterward show all three members 'started' and healthy at matching raft index 22 (cmd-ca7a137c0ac745d1).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-d2900fdd3d934d1e`, `cmd-e0a3fe2633864dd5`, `cmd-eca00e8542c14fd5`, `cmd-ca7a137c0ac745d1`
- **req-4 — Satisfied:** Existing application keys intact on the replaced node3 member after resync
  - **Why:** Querying /app --prefix directly against the new node3 member returns all four original keys with correct values, confirming full data resync from the surviving members (cmd-1a46e4a98d7647e8).
  - **Recorded evidence:** `cmd-1a46e4a98d7647e8`

### Operational hygiene

The verifier assigned hygiene **0.850**. All state-changing commands trace clearly to bootstrapping the cluster, simulating the node3 loss, replacing the member, or the mandated restart protocol — no unexplained troubleshooting mutations, failed services, or weakened security controls were observed. The one minor issue is unremoved installation artifacts (/tmp/etcd.tar.gz, /tmp/etcd-v3.7.1-linux-amd64/, /tmp/reboot.log) left on all three nodes after the task, confirmed still present in the after_executor snapshot; this is low-risk residue in /tmp rather than a functional or security problem, but it was never cleaned up.

Hygiene evidence: `cmd-caa62242d2184953`, `cmd-8a354ca6ae434a63`, `cmd-f2b42f50ece443bb`, `global:after_executor:node1:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node2:temporary-files`, `global:after_executor:node3:temporary-files`

### Comments and limitations

- after_prepare snapshot is an alias of before_prepare (prepare disabled), so preparer-vs-executor state separation relies entirely on the before_prepare vs after_executor comparison.
- Health/status checks rely on etcdctl output reported by the same session that performed the mutations; no fully independent third-party verification tool was used, though the checks are direct commands against the running cluster.
